title: Take apart: an interactive page that separates the Patch One layer by layer from one simulation model

Loopback to builder: The spec addendum (Kit adoption) requires the builder's output to state which kit conventions it relied on or adjusted, and to say whether any kit file was copied. runs/wo-gh-9/builder.output.md is 386 bytes and never mentions the kit, .anvil-factory/third_party/teardown, or a design system question. This requirement is unmet.; The Typography section sets body text at 17 px and gauge and data values at 32 to 56 px. src/take-apart-page.js still uses 12, 13, 16 and 22 px text for the caption, units, control headings, the header link, the JS-off fallback note and the temperature unit. No test asserts type sizes, so conformance to the design system sizes is unproven.; Minor: the tour cursor is 25 px wide with a 5 px box-shadow, off the 8 px rhythm. This is non-text and arguably outside the spacing rule.; Checked and met: the colour hexes in the page, client and capture script are all documented tokens, with none of the four substituted values. The font link, skip link, focusable main (tabindex -1), 3 px focus ring, 1440 px container and noscript fallback (layer list plus gaugeReadout(0)) are present in the page.; Checked and met: SETUP_COMMIT is 7748273, the harness files are excluded in the scope test, and the line leaves src/page.js unchanged, with one /take-apart anchor already in the baseline. The changed non-evidence files are only the four allowed ones.; Checked and met: evidence/take-apart/browser-pass.log exists and records 0 console errors and a PASS gauge comparison at hour 200. tests/take-apart.test.js passes 23 of 23 (I re-ran it). In the builder's suite log the only failure is test 98, the pre-existing S11 design-v4 test, which the spec carves out.; I found no injection surface. src/take-apart-client.js has no innerHTML, eval, new Function, document.write or insertAdjacent. The only input it reads is `location.search` for `tour=fast`, and that value is compared to a literal and never rendered. src/take-apart-page.js interpolates only FACTS.product and gaugeReadout(0), which are server-side constants. The page has no cookies, storage, fetch calls or postMessage.; The new routes in src/index.js (/take-apart, /take-apart-model.js, /take-apart.js, /vendor/three.module.min.js) are fixed paths that serve in-repo strings. Nothing in them is derived from the request, so there is no path traversal or open redirect. I did not check whether they accept non-GET methods. The existing handlers do not restrict them either, so that is not a regression.; src/vendor-three.js is labelled as the unmodified three.js 0.160.0 npm build under the MIT licence, and it is served from the same origin with an immutable cache. I did not recompute the hash of the decoded bytes, so the 'unmodified' claim is taken from the header comment. The immutable year-long cache on an unversioned URL means a later vendor bump will not reach cached clients. That is a deployment concern, not a security risk.; The only third-party origins are fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com. They are loaded through the same stylesheet link the main page uses, as the work order requires, and there is no other external script or CDN. The page sets no CSP or SRI, which matches the existing site posture. A CSP on the new routes would be a reasonable hardening step, but it is not required by the spec.; The noscript override is a static style block. It shows the layer list and the initial readings and does not weaken anything.; Scope check: git status shows no changes to src/facts.js, src/images.js or src/page.js. The run touches src/index.js, src/take-apart-*.js, tests and scripts, as allowed. Nothing sensitive is committed in the run logs or evidence that I could see.; I ran tests/take-apart.test.js: 23 of 23 pass. They cover model scenarios S1–S7, the browser twin, routes, S8 evidence, S9 payload sizes, S10 anchor and scope, and the loopback chrome assertions.; The builder's full-suite log (runs/wo-gh-9/builder-suite.log) shows 147 tests, 145 pass, 1 fail and 1 skipped. The only failure is test 98 in tests/design-v4-square-product.test.js (S11, patch-exploded / mounting not cleared). That is the itemized pre-existing failure, so it does not count against this run. I did not re-run the full suite myself.; Scope test: SETUP_COMMIT is '7748273', which is the head of this branch. The test excludes the four harness files (suite-output.txt, suite-result.txt, run-diff.txt, comment.md) from both the tracked diff and the untracked list before applying the allowed list. The tracked diff against 7748273 names no file outside the allowed scope. That diff includes the deletion of runs/wo-gh-9/reviewer-tests.output.md, which sits under the allowed runs/wo-gh-9/ path.; The src/page.js assertion is re-based to expect an empty diff against the setup commit. The served-HTML anchor test (S10) separately checks for exactly one /take-apart anchor labelled 'Take apart'. This matches the addendum.; The chrome tests are real and map to the mandate. They check for token-only hex colours in the page, client and capture sources, and the four substituted values are explicitly banned. They compute WCAG contrast for the documented pairs, with a 4.5 floor. They also check the font link with preconnect and swap, the skip link to a focusable main, the noscript content (explanation, layers, gaugeReadout(0), fallback note, override), the 1440 px container and the 3 px focus rings.; Evidence tests check that the five beat stills and the contact sheet are PNGs of at least 20 KB. They also check that browser-pass.log exists and records zero console errors, a passing gauge comparison and the vendor size. The committed log reads: console errors 0, gauge comparison PASS at hour 200, vendor decoded bytes 670681.; Minor weakness: both scope tests and the src/page.js test return silently when the setup commit is unreachable, for example in a shallow checkout. Scope enforcement then falls to the run gate. It is acceptable here because the commit resolves in this workspace, but it can hide a vacuous pass elsewhere.; Minor weakness: the chrome tests check that the 44 px targets, 8 px gaps and 18–20 px / 17 px / 32–56 px sizing are declared only indirectly, if at all. I did not find dedicated assertions for them. This does not block the pass, since the listed measurable items are covered.; I did not run the test suite. I checked the diff and the page source only.; Scope fits the spec's allowed list. The working-tree diff against HEAD touches only scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs, src/take-apart-client.js, src/take-apart-page.js and tests/take-apart.test.js, plus run and evidence files. src/page.js, src/index.js, src/facts.js and src/images.js are unchanged, as the spec's re-based diff assertion expects. The one nav anchor already exists in the baseline.; The simulation model stays the single source for page content. Layer names and thicknesses, the initial gauge values from gaugeReadout(0) and FACTS.wearDays are all rendered into src/take-apart-page.js from the model and facts. No gauge text is hardcoded.; The noscript content meets the spec. The static layer list and the visible fallback note are forced visible by the noscript style override, and the live controls are hidden. This follows the spec's no-script requirement.; The chrome follows the spec addendum. The :root tokens are only the documented set: paper, ink, teal, the #53685C secondary, hairline, body and mint. None of the four substituted hex values (#163c34, #008d7f, #6a7972, #dce1d9) remain in the three take-apart files I grepped. The Google Fonts link matches the spec (Inter 400/500, Space Grotesk 300/400/500, display=swap). The container is capped at max-width 1440px, and there is a skip link to a focusable main (tabindex=-1). Focus rings are 3px, and buttons, links and range inputs have a 44px minimum target with 8px gaps.; evidence/take-apart/browser-pass.log is present and records 'console errors: 0' and 'gauge comparison: PASS at hour 200'. This satisfies the committed-evidence item. The vendored three.js bytes decode to 670681 bytes. The log is untracked in the working tree, so the gate must commit it.; Minor, not blocking: the mono labels use the generic font-family:monospace, because the design system's mono face is not loaded on this page. That matches the spec's 11px, 0.16em label rule but gives platform-dependent glyphs.; Minor, not blocking: the page still has an inline style attribute (margin-bottom:24px on the eyebrow in the panel) and large single-line CSS blocks. This is a maintainability note only; it does not affect the architecture, and the tests cover the hex-colour rule.; I could not confirm from the diff alone whether the builder's output states which kit conventions it relied on or adjusted, or that no kit file was copied into the repo. Reviewer-spec should confirm that statement. I saw no files copied from .anvil-factory in the changed-file list.; Typography requires correction in src/take-apart-page.js: the mobile h1 is 36px, below DESIGN.md's 56px mobile hero minimum, and #fallback uses 16px body copy instead of 17px. Set the documented sizes and heading leading; h1 currently inherits the body's 1.65 leading. The font stylesheet, 18px introduction, 32–56px gauges and display weight 300 are correct.; Palette and contrast: chrome, callouts, chart and contact-sheet labels use the documented tokens. The documented text/background pairs meet the 4.5:1 floor.; Spacing and container: fixed content spacing follows the 8px rhythm; the container is capped at 1440px and gutters use clamp(24px,5vw,80px).; Accessibility: the skip link targets main with tabindex=-1; 3px focus rings, 44px button and range targets, and 8px control gaps are declared. The supplied contact sheet establishes desktop appearance only; capture checks 390px overflow but does not establish the documented 320px and zoom quality bars.; No-script behavior: served HTML includes the explanation, five layer names and thicknesses, gaugeReadout(0) values, and a fallback note revealed by the noscript override. Correct the fallback typography noted above.; Assembled / Assemble: cleared under S11. Layers appear flush, labels identify the correct layers without covering them, and gauges show the hour-zero state.; Apart / Explode: cleared under S11. Five layers separate in order with model-consistent gaps, unobstructed labels and unchanged hour-zero gauges.; Board / Isolate the board: cleared under S11. The board is lifted and emphasized, other layers fade and step aside, and labels and gauges remain consistent.; X ray: cleared under S11. The cover fades further while the focused board remains visible; no unexpected intersection, misplaced label or gauge discrepancy is evident.; Mid / Settle: cleared under S11. The partially separated stack and released focus agree with the settle state; 36.9°C, hydration 69, battery 59% and day 7 agree with gaugeReadout(156).; Evidence completeness remains pending: evidence/take-apart/browser-pass.log records zero console errors and a passing hour-200 gauge comparison, but git status reports it as untracked. Include it in the committed evidence as required by the loopback addendum.
